record.context_brief: continuous subsolution implies continuous solution locally
record.original_question: Let mu be a probability measure on a bounded domain Omega in C^n. Assume there exists a continuous plurisubharmonic subsolution u on Omega with u|_{partial Omega} = 0 and mu <= (dd^c u)^n in Omega. Determine whether there must exist a continuous plurisubharmonic function phi on Omega with phi|_{partial Omega} = 0 and mu = (dd^c phi)^n in Omega.

evidence.quote: Question 14 (Kolodziej). Assume there is a continuous subsolution to the Dirichlet problem, i.e. there is a continuous psh function u in Omega such that u|_{partial Omega} = 0 and mu <= (dd^c u)^n in Omega. Does it imply that there is a continuous solution, i.e. a continuous psh function phi such that phi|_{partial Omega} = 0 and mu = (dd^c phi)^n in Omega ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a bounded strictly pseudoconvex domain, and let $\mu$ be a non-negative Borel (probability) measure on $\Omega$. For a plurisubharmonic function $v$ on $\Omega$ that is locally bounded, the complex Monge-Ampère operator $(dd^c v)^n$ is defined in the sense of Bedford-Taylor as a non-negative Borel measure on $\Omega$, where $d = \partial + \bar\partial$ and $d^c = i(\bar\partial - \partial)$.

Suppose there exists a continuous plurisubharmonic function $u : \overline{\Omega} \to \mathbb{R}$ (a "continuous subsolution") satisfying
$$u\big|_{\partial \Omega} = 0 \qquad \text{and} \qquad \mu \le (dd^c u)^n \text{ in } \Omega.$$

Question: Must there then exist a continuous plurisubharmonic function $\varphi : \overline{\Omega} \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfying
$$\varphi\big|_{\partial \Omega} = 0 \qquad \text{and} \qquad (dd^c \varphi)^n = \mu \text{ in } \Omega ?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The general "continuous subsolution problem" attributed to Kołodziej is reported as still open. Partial results are known: Kołodziej and Nguyen (arXiv:1808.07197) proved that if the subsolution's modulus of continuity satisfies a Dini-type condition, then a continuous solution to the Dirichlet problem exists; further refinements have appeared on Hermitian manifolds and for measures dominated by capacity.

status_evidence.title: A Remark on the Continuous Subsolution Problem for the Complex Monge-Ampère Equation
status_evidence.snippet: It is still an open problem whether a continuous subsolution implies solvability of the Dirichlet problem; we prove it under a Dini-type condition on the modulus of continuity.
status_evidence.claim: The general problem is open; a Dini-type modulus-of-continuity condition on the subsolution suffices.

status_evidence.title: Continuous solutions to Monge–Ampère equations on Hermitian manifolds for measures dominated by capacity
status_evidence.snippet: Continuous solutions are obtained when the measure is locally dominated by capacity.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results obtained under capacity-domination hypotheses.
